chosen_title: SpaceX shares extend slide with another 3% fall; over $600 billion in market value wiped out in 3 sessions
caption:
🚀 SpaceX just had one of the most dramatic post-IPO crashes in Wall Street history.

Within three trading sessions of going public, SpaceX shares plunged so sharply that over $600 billion in market value was erased — pushing the stock below its own listing price. That is a historic wipeout by almost any measure.

The selloff was driven by three fears hitting simultaneously: an IPO valuation many analysts already considered stretched, mounting investor anxiety about the company's heavy debt-funded push into AI infrastructure, and a broader wave of selling hammering tech stocks across Wall Street. SpaceX had long been the crown jewel of private markets — but public markets play by colder rules.

A 5% rebound followed as bargain hunters stepped in, though shares remained below their IPO listing price — meaning anyone who bought on day one is still underwater.

Why it matters: This is the sharpest possible reality check for the 'growth at any price' era of AI investing. Even the world's most iconic companies are not immune to the cold logic of public market valuations.

Source: Markets — Economic Times / CNBC

slides.headline: $600 BILLION gone in 3 days

slides.label: THE STORY
slides.headline: SpaceX IPO'd — then the floor dropped
slides.body: After one of the most anticipated stock market debuts in years, SpaceX shares tumbled across three consecutive sessions, erasing over $600 billion in market value and pushing the stock below its own listing price. The selling was driven by concerns over the company's lofty post-IPO valuation, its heavy reliance on debt-funded AI spending, and a broader technology selloff sweeping Wall Street. A 5% rebound followed as bargain hunters stepped in — but shares remained underwater for anyone who bought on IPO day.

slides.art_prompt: A sweating cartoon bull wearing a Wall Street tie, slumped at a trading desk surrounded by towering glowing AI server racks plastered with giant credit-card bills and price tags, a massive red arrow smashing down through the ceiling above him, a small SpaceX rocket model on the desk with an 'OVERVALUED' sticker slapped on it, flat lime-green and white comic style, high energy
slides.headline: AI debt fears spooked the market
slides.body: Investors punished SpaceX for betting heavily on AI infrastructure funded by borrowed money — a strategy that dazzled private-market backers but rattled public shareholders as the Federal Reserve held rates high and tech valuations came under scrutiny.

slides.label: THE NUMBER
slides.caption: Over $600 billion in SpaceX market value was wiped out across just three trading sessions — a short-term market-cap destruction larger than the total value of most Fortune 500 companies.

slides.label: WHY IT MATTERS
points: SpaceX's IPO was among the most anticipated public offerings in years, giving everyday retail investors their first chance to own a piece of Elon Musk's rocket and AI company.
Losing $600 billion in market cap across three sessions is a historically rare event — the scale rivals some of the largest single-stock crashes ever recorded on Wall Street.
The selloff signals a wider investor reckoning: technology companies that borrow aggressively to fund AI expansion are facing growing punishment in a high-interest-rate environment.
Despite the 5% single-day rebound driven by bargain hunters, SpaceX shares remained below their listing price, leaving IPO-day buyers sitting on paper losses.
